349: 
350:           def extract_settings_user_opt_in_from_text(rollout_state: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
351:               """
352:               Extracts the text with settings, if any, and the opted in users from the rollout state.
353: 
354:               If the issue body contains "---" then the text above that is the settings
355:               and the text below is the list of opted in users.
356: 
357:               If it doesn't contain "---" then the settings are empty and the rest is the users.
358:               """
359:               rollout_state_parts = rollout_state.split("---")
360:               if len(rollout_state_parts) >= 2:
361:                   return rollout_state_parts[0], rollout_state_parts[1]
362:               else:
363:                   return "", rollout_state
364: 
365: 
366:           class UserOptins(dict[str, list[str]]):
367:               """
368:               Dictionary of users with a list of features they have opted into
369:               """
370: 
371: 
372:           def parse_user_opt_in_from_text(user_optin_text: str) -> UserOptins:
373:               """
374:               Parse the user opt-in text into a key value pair of username and the list of features they have opted into
375: 
376:               Users are GitHub usernames with the @ prefix. Each user is also a comma-separated list of features/experiments to enable.
377:                   - Example line: "@User1,lf,split_build"
378:                   - A "#" prefix indicates the user is opted out of all experiments
379: 
380: 
381:               """
382:               optins = UserOptins()
383:               for user in user_optin_text.split("\n"):
384:                   user = user.strip("\r\n\t -")
385:                   if not user or not user.startswith("@"):
386:                       # Not a valid user. Skip
387:                       continue
388: 
389:                   if user:
390:                       usr_name = user.split(",")[0].strip("@")
391:                       optins[usr_name] = [exp.strip(" ") for exp in user.split(",")[1:]]
392: 
393:               return optins
394: 
395: 
396:           def is_valid_experiment_name(experiment_name: str) -> bool:
397:               """
398:               Check if the experiment name is valid.
399:               A valid name:
400:                   - Contains only alphanumeric characters and the special characters "_" & "-"
401:                   - The special characters "_" & "-" shouldn't be the first or last characters
402:                   - Cannot contain spaces
403:               """
404: 
405:               valid_char_regex = r"^[a-zA-Z0-9]([\w-]*[a-zA-Z0-9])?$"
406:               valid = bool(re.match(valid_char_regex, experiment_name))
407: 
408:               if valid:
409:                   return True
410: 
411:               log.error(
412:                   f"Invalid experiment name: {experiment_name}. Experiment names should only contain alphanumeric characters, '_', and '-'. They cannot contain spaces, and the special characters '_' and '-' cannot be the first or last characters."
413:               )
414:               return False
415: 
416: 
417:           def parse_settings_from_text(settings_text: str) -> Settings:
418:               """
419:               Parse the experiments from the issue body into a list of ExperimentSettings
420:               """
421:               try:
422:                   if settings_text:
423:                       # Escape the backtick as well so that we can have the settings in a code block on the GH issue
424:                       # for easy reading
425:                       # Note: Using ascii for the backtick so that the cat step in _runner-determinator.yml doesn't choke on
426:                       #       the backtick character in shell commands.
427:                       backtick = chr(96)  # backtick character
428:                       settings_text = settings_text.strip(f"\r\n\t{backtick} ")
429:                       settings = load_yaml(settings_text)
430: 
431:                       # For now we just load experiments. We can expand this if/when we add more settings
432:                       experiments = {}
433: 
434:                       for exp_name, exp_settings in settings.get(SETTING_EXPERIMENTS).items():
435:                           if not is_valid_experiment_name(exp_name):
436:                               # Exclude invalid experiments from the list. We log an error, but don't raise an exception so that other experiments can still be processed.
437:                               continue
438: 
439:                           valid_settings = {}
440:                           for setting in exp_settings:
441:                               if setting not in Experiment._fields:
442:                                   log.warning(
443:                                       f"Unexpected setting in experiment: {setting} = {exp_settings[setting]}"
444:                                   )
445:                               else:
446:                                   valid_settings[setting] = exp_settings[setting]
447: 
448:                           experiments[exp_name] = Experiment(**valid_settings)
449:                       return Settings(experiments)
450: 
451:               except Exception:
452:                   log.exception("Failed to parse settings")
453: 
454:               return Settings()
455: 
456: 
457:           def parse_settings(rollout_state: str) -> Settings:
458:               """
459:               Parse settings, if any, from the rollout state.
460: 
461:               If the issue body contains "---" then the text above that is the settings
462:               and the text below is the list of opted in users.
463: 
464:               If it doesn't contain "---" then the settings are empty and the default values are used.
465:               """
466:               settings_text, _ = extract_settings_user_opt_in_from_text(rollout_state)
467:               return parse_settings_from_text(settings_text)
468: 
469: 
470:           def parse_users(rollout_state: str) -> UserOptins:
471:               """
472:               Parse users from the rollout state.
473: 
474:               """
475:               _, users_text = extract_settings_user_opt_in_from_text(rollout_state)
476:               return parse_user_opt_in_from_text(users_text)
477: 
478: 
479:           def is_user_opted_in(user: str, user_optins: UserOptins, experiment_name: str) -> bool:
480:               """
481:               Check if a user is opted into an experiment
482:               """
483:               return experiment_name in user_optins.get(user, [])
484: 
485: 
486:           def is_user_opted_out(user: str, user_optins: UserOptins, experiment_name: str) -> bool:
487:               """
488:               Check if a user explicitly opted out of an experiment
489:               """
490:               # if the experiment is prefixed with a "-", then it's an opt-out
491:               experiment_optout = "-" + experiment_name
492:               if experiment_optout not in user_optins.get(user, []):
493:                   return False
494: 
495:               if is_user_opted_in(user, user_optins, experiment_name):
496:                   log.warning(
497:                       f"User {user} is opted into experiment {experiment_name}, but also opted out of it. Defaulting to opting out"
498:                   )
499: 
500:               return True
501: 
502: 
503:           def get_runner_prefix(
504:               rollout_state: str,
505:               workflow_requestors: Iterable[str],
506:               branch: str,
507:               eligible_experiments: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
508:               opt_out_experiments: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
509:               is_canary: bool = False,
510:           ) -> str:
511:               settings = parse_settings(rollout_state)
512:               user_optins = parse_users(rollout_state)
513: 
514:               fleet_prefix = ""
515:               prefixes = []
516:               for experiment_name, experiment_settings in settings.experiments.items():
517:                   if not experiment_settings.all_branches and is_exception_branch(branch):
518:                       log.info(
519:                           f"Branch {branch} is an exception branch. Not enabling experiment {experiment_name}."
520:                       )
521:                       continue
522: 
523:                   if opt_out_experiments:
524:                       if experiment_name in opt_out_experiments:
525:                           opt_out_exp_list = ", ".join(opt_out_experiments)
526:                           log.info(
527:                               f"Skipping experiment '{experiment_name}', as this workflow has opted-out (opted out experiments are: {opt_out_exp_list})"
528:                           )
529:                           continue
530: 
531:                   if eligible_experiments:
532:                       if experiment_name not in eligible_experiments:
533:                           exp_list = ", ".join(eligible_experiments)
534:                           log.info(
535:                               f"Skipping experiment '{experiment_name}', as it is not in the eligible_experiments list: {exp_list}"
536:                           )
537:                           continue
538:                   elif not experiment_settings.default:
539:                       log.info(

2: # Workflow that runs lint checks and also unittests for tools, and scripts.
3: 
4: on:
5:   pull_request:
6:     branches-ignore:
7:       - nightly
8:   push:
9:     branches:
10:       - main
11:       - release/*
12:       - landchecks/*
13:     tags:
14:       - ciflow/pull/*
15:       - ciflow/trunk/*
16:   workflow_dispatch:
17: 
18: permissions: read-all
19: # The names of steps that actually test the code should be suffixed with `(nonretryable)`.
20: # When any other step fails, it's job will be retried once by retryBot.
21: jobs:
22:   get-label-type:
23:     if: github.repository_owner == 'pytorch'
24:     name: get-label-type
25:     uses: pytorch/pytorch/.github/workflows/_runner-determinator.yml@main
26:     with:
27:       triggering_actor: ${{ github.triggering_actor }}
28:       issue_owner: ${{ github.event.pull_request.user.login || github.event.issue.user.login }}
29:       curr_branch: ${{ github.head_ref || github.ref_name }}
30: 
31:   get-changed-files:
32:     if: github.repository_owner == 'pytorch'
33:     name: Get changed files
34:     uses: ./.github/workflows/_get-changed-files.yml
35:     with:
36:       all_files: ${{ contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'lint-all-files') || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'Reverted') || github.event_name == 'push' }}
37: 
38:   lintrunner-clang:
39:     uses: pytorch/test-infra/.github/workflows/linux_job_v2.yml@main
40:     # Needed to prevent deduping on HUD
41:     name: lintrunner-clang-${{ needs.get-changed-files.outputs.changed-files == '*' && 'all' || 'partial' }}

32: jobs:

48:           GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

51:     needs: get_workflow_conclusion
52:     if: github.repository_owner == 'pytorch'
53:     runs-on: ubuntu-22.04
54:     environment: upload-stats
55:     permissions:
56:       id-token: write
57:     name: Upload test stats for ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}, attempt ${{ github.event.workflow_run.run_attempt }}
58:     steps:
59:       - name: Print workflow information
60:         env:
61:           TRIGGERING_WORKFLOW: ${{ toJSON(github.event.workflow_run) }}

63: 
64:       - name: Checkout PyTorch
65:         uses: pytorch/pytorch/.github/actions/checkout-pytorch@main
66: 
67:       - name: Configure aws credentials
68:         uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@ececac1a45f3b08a01d2dd070d28d111c5fe6722 # v4.1.0
69:         continue-on-error: true
70:         with:
71:           role-to-assume: arn:aws:iam::308535385114:role/gha_workflow_upload-torch-test-stats
72:           aws-region: us-east-1
73: 
74:       - uses: actions/setup-python@a26af69be951a213d495a4c3e4e4022e16d87065 # v5.6.0
75:         with:
76:           python-version: '3.11'
77:           cache: pip
78: 
79:       - run: |
80:           pip3 install requests==2.32.2 boto3==1.35.42
81: 
82:       - name: Upload test artifacts
83:         id: upload-s3
84:         env:
85:           GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
86:           WORKFLOW_ARTIFACTS_URL: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.artifacts_url }}
87:           WORKFLOW_RUN_ID: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
88:           WORKFLOW_RUN_ATTEMPT: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.run_attempt }}
89:           REPO_FULLNAME: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.repository.full_name }}
90:         run: |
91:           echo "${WORKFLOW_ARTIFACTS_URL}"
92: 
93:           # Note that in the case of Linux and Windows, their artifacts have already been uploaded to S3, so there simply won't be
94:           # anything on GitHub to upload. The command should return right away
95:           python3 -m tools.stats.upload_artifacts --workflow-run-id "${WORKFLOW_RUN_ID}" --workflow-run-attempt "${WORKFLOW_RUN_ATTEMPT}" --repo "${REPO_FULLNAME}"
96: 
97:       - name: Upload test stats
98:         env:
99:           GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
100:           WORKFLOW_RUN_ID: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}
101:           WORKFLOW_RUN_ATTEMPT: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.run_attempt }}
102:           WORKFLOW_URL: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.html_url }}
103:           HEAD_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name }}
104:           HEAD_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch }}
105:         run: |
106:           echo "${WORKFLOW_URL}"
107:           python3 -m tools.stats.upload_test_stats --workflow-run-id "${WORKFLOW_RUN_ID}" --workflow-run-attempt "${WORKFLOW_RUN_ATTEMPT}" --head-branch "${HEAD_BRANCH}" --head-repository "${HEAD_REPOSITORY}"
108:           python3 -m tools.stats.upload_sccache_stats --workflow-run-id "${WORKFLOW_RUN_ID}" --workflow-run-attempt "${WORKFLOW_RUN_ATTEMPT}"
109: 
110:       - name: Analyze disabled tests rerun
111:         env:
112:           GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
113:           WORKFLOW_ARTIFACTS_URL: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.artifacts_url }}
114:           WORKFLOW_RUN_ID: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}

126:           REPO_FULLNAME: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.repository.full_name }}

    data = json.load(f)

# For files where added != deleted, show the full diff body
for file in data['files']:
    if file['added'] != file['deleted']:
        print(f"\n=== {file['path']} (+{file['added']} -{file['deleted']}) ===")
        for hunk in file['hunks']:
            print(hunk['body'])
EOF

142:           # anymore

145:           DOCS_TYPE: ${{ matrix.docs_type }}
146:           RUN_DOXYGEN: ${{ inputs.run-doxygen }}
147:           BUILD_ENVIRONMENT: ${{ inputs.build-environment }}
148:         run: |

{"content":"1: name: linux-build
2: 
3: on:
4:   workflow_call:
5:     inputs:
6:       build-environment:
7:         required: true
8:         type: string
9:         description: Top-level label for what's being built/tested.
10:       docker-image-name:
11:         required: true
12:         type: string
13:         description: Name of the base docker image to build with.
14:       build-generates-artifacts:
15:         required: false
16:         type: boolean
17:         default: true
18:         description: If set, upload generated build artifacts.
19:       sync-tag:
20:         required: false
21:         type: string
22:         default: ""
23:         description: |
24:           If this is set, our linter will use this to make sure that every other
25:           job with the same `sync-tag` is identical.
26:       cuda-arch-list:
27:         required: false
28:         type: string
29:         default: "5.2"
30:         description: |
31:           List of CUDA architectures CI build should target.
32:       runner_prefix:
33:         required: false
34:         default: ""
35:         type: string
36:         description: Prefix for runner label
37:       runner:
38:         required: false
39:         type: string
40:         default: "linux.c7i.2xlarge"
41:         description: |
42:           Label of the runner this job should run on.
43:       test-matrix:
44:         required: false
45:         type: string
46:         description: |
47:           An option JSON description of what test configs to run later on. This
48:           is moved here from the Linux test workflow so that we can apply filter
49:           logic using test-config labels earlier and skip unnecessary builds
50:       selected-test-configs:
51:         description: |
52:           A comma-separated list of test configurations from the test matrix to keep,
53:           The empty list means we are going to keep every configurations by defaults
54:         required: false
55:         type: string
56:         default: ""
57:       s3-bucket:
58:         description: S3 bucket to download artifact
59:         required: false
60:         type: string
61:         default: "gha-artifacts"
62:       aws-role-to-assume:
63:         description: Role to assume for downloading artifacts
64:         required: false
65:         type: string
66:         default: ""
67:       disable-monitor:
68:         description: |
69:           Disable utilization monitoring for build job
70:         required: false
71:         type: boolean
72:         default: false
73:       monitor-log-interval:
74:         description: |
75:           Set the interval for the monitor script to log utilization.
76:         required: false
77:         type: number
78:         default: 5
79:       monitor-data-collect-interval:
80:         description: |
81:           Set the interval for the monitor script to collect data.
82:         required: false
83:         type: number
84:         default: 1
85:       allow-reuse-old-whl:
86:         description: |
87:           If set, the build try to pull an old wheel from s3 that was built on a
88:           commit with no cpp changes from this commit
89:         required: false
90:         type: boolean
91:         default: true
92:       build-additional-packages:
93:         description: |
94:           If set, the build job will also builds these packages and saves their
95:           wheels as artifacts
96:         required: false
97:         type: string
98:         default: ""
99:       build-external-packages:
100:         description: |
101:           If set, the build external packages and saves their wheels as artifacts
102:           use command separated list of packages to build ex: 'vllm,transformers'.
103:         required: false
104:         type: string
105:         default: ""
106: 
107:     secrets:
108:       HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN:
109:         required: false
110:         description: |
111:           HF Auth token to avoid rate limits when downloading models or datasets from hub
112:       SCRIBE_GRAPHQL_ACCESS_TOKEN:
113:         required: false
114:         description: |
115:           FB app token to write to scribe endpoint
116: 
117:     outputs:
118:       docker-image:
119:         value: ${{ jobs.build.outputs.docker-image }}
120:         description: The docker image containing the built PyTorch.
121:       test-matrix:
122:         value: ${{ jobs.build.outputs.test-matrix }}
123:         description: An optional JSON description of what test configs to run later on.
124:       build-environment:
125:         value: ${{ jobs.build.outputs.build-environment }}
126:         description: Top-level label for what's being built/tested.
127: 
128: jobs:
129:   build:
130:     environment: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && 'scribe-protected' || startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/release/') && 'scribe-protected' || contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'ci-scribe') && 'scribe-pr' || '' }}
131:     # Don't run on forked repos
132:     if: github.repository_owner == 'pytorch'
133:     runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner_prefix}}${{ inputs.runner }}
134:     timeout-minutes: 480
135:     outputs:
136:       docker-image: ${{ steps.calculate-docker-image.outputs.docker-image }}
137:       test-matrix: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.test-matrix }}
138:       build-environment: ${{ inputs.build-environment }}
139:     steps:
140:       - name: Setup SSH (Click me for login details)
141:         uses: pytorch/test-infra/.github/actions/setup-ssh@main
142:         if: inputs.build-environment != 'linux-s390x-binary-manywheel'
143:         with:
144:           github-secret: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
145:           instructions: |
146:             Build is done inside the container, to start an interactive session run:
147:               docker exec -it $(docker container ps --format '{{.ID}}') bash
148: 
149:       # [pytorch repo ref]
150:       # Use a pytorch/pytorch reference instead of a reference to the local
151:       # checkout because when we run this action we don't *have* a local
152:       # checkout. In other cases you should prefer a local checkout.
153:       - name: Checkout PyTorch
154:         uses: pytorch/pytorch/.github/actions/checkout-pytorch@main
155:         with:
156:           no-sudo: true
157: 
158:       - name: Setup Linux
159:         uses: ./.github/actions/setup-linux
160:         if: inputs.build-environment != 'linux-s390x-binary-manywheel'
161: 
162:       - name: configure aws credentials
163:         uses: aws-actions/configure-aws-credentials@ececac1a45f3b08a01d2dd070d28d111c5fe6722 # v4.1.0
164:         if: ${{ inputs.aws-role-to-assume != '' && inputs.build-environment != 'linux-s390x-binary-manywheel' }}
165:         with:
166:           role-to-assume: ${{ inputs.aws-role-to-assume }}
167:           role-session-name: gha-linux-build
168:           aws-region: us-east-1
169: 
170:       - name: Get workflow job id
171:         id: get-job-id
172:         uses: ./.github/actions/get-workflow-job-id
173:         if: always()
174:         with:
175:           github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
176: 
177:       - name: Check if can use old whl build
178:         id: use-old-whl
179:         uses: ./.github/actions/reuse-old-whl
180:         if: ${{ inputs.allow-reuse-old-whl }}
181:         with:
182:           build-environment: ${{ inputs.build-environment }}
183:           run-id: ${{ github.run_id }}
184:           github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
185:           job-id: ${{ steps.get-job-id.outputs.job-id }}
186:           job-name: ${{ steps.get-job-id.outputs.job-name }}
187: 
188:       - name: Calculate docker image
189:         id: calculate-docker-image
190:         uses: pytorch/test-infra/.github/actions/calculate-docker-image@main
191:         if: inputs.build-environment != 'linux-s390x-binary-manywheel'
192:         with:
193:           docker-image-name: ${{ inputs.docker-image-name }}
194: 
195:       - name: Use following to pull public copy of the image
196:         id: print-ghcr-mirror
197:         if: inputs.build-environment != 'linux-s390x-binary-manywheel' && steps.use-old-whl.outputs.reuse != 'true'
198:         env:
199:           ECR_DOCKER_IMAGE: ${{ steps.calculate-docker-image.outputs.docker-image }}
200:         shell: bash
201:         run: |
202:           tag=${ECR_DOCKER_IMAGE##*:}
203:           echo "docker pull ghcr.io/pytorch/ci-image:${tag/:/-}"
204: 
205:       - name: Pull docker image
206:         uses: pytorch/test-infra/.github/actions/pull-docker-image@main
207:         if: inputs.build-environment != 'linux-s390x-binary-manywheel' && steps.use-old-whl.outputs.reuse != 'true'
208:         with:
209:           docker-image: ${{ steps.calculate-docker-image.outputs.docker-image }}
210: 
211:       - name: Parse ref
212:         id: parse-ref
213:         run: .github/scripts/parse_ref.py
214: 
215:       # Apply the filter logic to the build step too if the test-config label is already there
216:       - name: Select all requested test configurations (if the test matrix is available)
217:         id: filter
218:         uses: ./.github/actions/filter-test-configs
219:         with:
220:           github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
221:           test-matrix: ${{ inputs.test-matrix }}
222:           selected-test-configs: ${{ inputs.selected-test-configs }}
223:           job-name: ${{ steps.get-job-id.outputs.job-name }}
224: 
225:       - name: Start monitoring script
226:         id: monitor-script
227:         if: ${{ !inputs.disable-monitor }}
228:         shell: bash
229:         continue-on-error: true
230:         env:
231:           JOB_ID: ${{ steps.get-job-id.outputs.job-id }}
232:           JOB_NAME: ${{ steps.get-job-id.outputs.job-name }}
233:           WORKFLOW_NAME: ${{ github.workflow }}
234:           WORKFLOW_RUN_ID: ${{github.run_id}}
235:           MONITOR_LOG_INTERVAL: ${{ inputs.monitor-log-interval }}
236:           MONITOR_DATA_COLLECT_INTERVAL: ${{ inputs.monitor-data-collect-interval }}
237:         run: |
238:           mkdir -p ../../usage_logs
239:           python3 -m pip install psutil==5.9.8 dataclasses_json==0.6.7
240:           python3 -m tools.stats.monitor \
241:           --log-interval "$MONITOR_LOG_INTERVAL" \
242:           --data-collect-interval "$MONITOR_DATA_COLLECT_INTERVAL" \
243:           > "../../usage_logs/usage_log_build_${JOB_ID}.txt" 2>&1 &
244:           echo "monitor-script-pid=${!}" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
245: 
246:       - name: Download pytest cache
247:         uses: ./.github/actions/pytest-cache-download
248:         continue-on-error: true
249:         if: inputs.build-environment != 'linux-s390x-binary-manywheel' && steps.use-old-whl.outputs.reuse != 'true'
250:         with:
251:           cache_dir: .pytest_cache
252:           job_identifier: ${{ github.workflow }}_${{ inputs.build-environment }}
253:           s3_bucket: ${{ inputs.s3-bucket }}
254: 
255:       - name: Build
256:         if: (steps.filter.outputs.is-test-matrix-empty == 'False' || inputs.test-matrix == '') && steps.use-old-whl.outputs.reuse != 'true'
257:         id: build
258:         env:
259:           BUILD_ENVIRONMENT: ${{ inputs.build-environment }}
260:           BRANCH: ${{ steps.parse-ref.outputs.branch }}
261:           PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
262:           SHA1: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
263:           # Do not set SCCACHE_S3_KEY_PREFIX to share the cache between all build jobs
264:           SCCACHE_BUCKET: ossci-compiler-cache-circleci-v2
265:           SCCACHE_REGION: us-east-1
266:           XLA_CLANG_CACHE_S3_BUCKET_NAME: ossci-compiler-clang-cache-circleci-xla
267:           PR_LABELS: ${{ toJson(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name) }}
268:           TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST: ${{ inputs.cuda-arch-list }}
269:           DOCKER_IMAGE: ${{ steps.calculate-docker-image.outputs.docker-image }}
270:           DOCKER_IMAGE_S390X: ${{ inputs.docker-image-name }}
271:           XLA_CUDA: ${{ contains(inputs.build-environment, 'xla') && '0' || '' }}
272:           OUR_GITHUB_JOB_ID: ${{ steps.get-job-id.outputs.job-id }}
273:           HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN }}
274:           SCRIBE_GRAPHQL_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SCRIBE_GRAPHQL_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
275:           BUILD_ADDITIONAL_PACKAGES: ${{ inputs.build-additional-packages }}
276:           RUNNER: ${{ inputs.runner }}
277:         run: |
278:           START_TIME=$(date +%s)
279:           if [[ ${BUILD_ENVIRONMENT} == *"s390x"* ]]; then
280:             JENKINS_USER=
281:             USED_IMAGE="${DOCKER_IMAGE_S390X}"
282:             # ensure that docker container cleanly exits in 12 hours
283:             # if for some reason cleanup action doesn't stop container
284:             # when job is cancelled
285:             DOCKER_SHELL_CMD="sleep 12h"
286: 
287:             # since some steps are skipped on s390x, if they are necessary, run them here
288:             env | grep '^GITHUB' >> "/tmp/github_env_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
289:             env | grep '^CI' >> "/tmp/github_env_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
290:           else
291:             JENKINS_USER="--user jenkins"
292:             USED_IMAGE="${DOCKER_IMAGE}"
293:             DOCKER_SHELL_CMD=
294:           fi
295: 
296:           # Leaving 1GB for the runner and other things

{"content":"1: # The point of this workflow is to test that a FA3 wheel that was built based off the
2: # stable ABI as of torch nightly 20250830 can still run on the newer torch.
3: #
4: # This workflow is very similar to the _linux-test.yml workflow, with the following
5: # differences:
6: #   1. It is simpler (there is no test matrix)
7: #   2. It pulls flash-attention as a secondary repository in order to access the tests.
8: #      Note that it does not BUILD anything from flash-attention, as we have a prebuilt
9: #      wheel. We pull flash-attention only to run a few tests.
10: #   3. It runs only FA3 tests. No PyTorch tests are run.
11: name: linux-test-stable-fa3
12: 
13: on:
14:   workflow_call:
15:     inputs:
16:       build-environment:
17:         required: true
18:         type: string
19:         description: Top-level label for what's being built/tested.
20:       docker-image:
21:         required: true
22:         type: string
23:         description: Docker image to run in.
24:       timeout-minutes:
25:         required: false
26:         type: number
27:         default: 30
28:         description: |
29:           Set the maximum (in minutes) how long the workflow should take to finish
30:       s3-bucket:
31:         description: S3 bucket to download artifact
32:         required: false
33:         type: string
34:         default: "gha-artifacts"
35:     secrets:
36:       HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN:
37:         required: false
38:         description: |
39:           HF Auth token to avoid rate limits when downloading models or datasets from hub
40:       VLLM_TEST_HUGGING_FACE_TOKEN:
41:         required: false
42:         description: |
43:           HF Auth token to test vllm
44:       SCRIBE_GRAPHQL_ACCESS_TOKEN:
45:         required: false
46:         description: |
47:           FB app token to write to scribe endpoint
48: 
49: env:
50:   GIT_DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
51: 
52: jobs:
53:   test:
54:     # Don't run on forked repos
55:     if: github.repository_owner == 'pytorch'
56:     runs-on: linux.aws.h100
57:     timeout-minutes: ${{ inputs.timeout-minutes || 30 }}
58:     permissions:
59:       id-token: write
60:       contents: read
61:     steps:
62:       - name: Checkout PyTorch
63:         uses: pytorch/pytorch/.github/actions/checkout-pytorch@main
64:         with:
65:           no-sudo: true
66: 
67:       - name: Checkout flash-attention as a secondary repository
68:         uses: actions/checkout@v4
69:         with:
70:           repository: Dao-AILab/flash-attention
71:           path: flash-attention
72: 
73:       - name: Setup Linux
74:         uses: ./.github/actions/setup-linux
75: 
76:       - name: Calculate docker image
77:         id: calculate-docker-image
78:         uses: pytorch/test-infra/.github/actions/calculate-docker-image@main
79:         with:
80:           docker-image-name: ${{ inputs.docker-image }}
81: 
82:       - name: Use following to pull public copy of the image
83:         id: print-ghcr-mirror
84:         env:
85:           ECR_DOCKER_IMAGE: ${{ steps.calculate-docker-image.outputs.docker-image }}
86:         shell: bash
87:         run: |
88:           tag=${ECR_DOCKER_IMAGE##*:}
89:           echo "docker pull ghcr.io/pytorch/ci-image:${tag/:/-}"
90: 
91:       - name: Pull docker image
92:         uses: pytorch/test-infra/.github/actions/pull-docker-image@main
93:         with:
94:           docker-image: ${{ steps.calculate-docker-image.outputs.docker-image }}
95: 
96:       - name: Check if in a container runner
97:         shell: bash
98:         id: check_container_runner
99:         run: echo "IN_CONTAINER_RUNNER=$(if [ -f /.inarc ] || [ -f /.incontainer ]; then echo true ; else echo false; fi)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
100: 
101:       - name: Setup GPU_FLAG for docker run
102:         id: setup-gpu-flag
103:         run: echo "GPU_FLAG=--gpus all -e NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=all" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
104: 
105:       - name: Setup SCCACHE_SERVER_PORT environment for docker run when on container
106:         id: setup-sscache-port-flag
107:         run: echo "SCCACHE_SERVER_PORT_DOCKER_FLAG=-e SCCACHE_SERVER_PORT=$((RUNNER_UID + 4226))" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
108:         if: ${{ steps.check_container_runner.outputs.IN_CONTAINER_RUNNER == 'true' }}
109: 
110:       - name: Get workflow job id
111:         id: get-job-id
112:         uses: ./.github/actions/get-workflow-job-id
113:         if: always()
114:         with:
115:           github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
116: 
117:       - name: Download build artifacts
118:         uses: ./.github/actions/download-build-artifacts
119:         with:
120:           name: ${{ inputs.build-environment }}
121:           s3-bucket: ${{ inputs.s3-bucket }}
122: 
123:       - name: Parse ref
124:         id: parse-ref
125:         run: .github/scripts/parse_ref.py
126: 
127:       - name: Set Test step time
128:         id: test-timeout
129:         shell: bash
130:         env:
131:           JOB_TIMEOUT: ${{ inputs.timeout-minutes }}
132:         run: |
133:           echo "timeout=$((JOB_TIMEOUT-30))" >> "${GITHUB_OUTPUT}"
134: 
135:       - name: Preserve github env variables for use in docker
136:         shell: bash
137:         run: |
138:           env | grep '^GITHUB' >> "/tmp/github_env_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
139:           env | grep '^CI' >> "/tmp/github_env_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
140: 
141:       - name: Test
142:         id: test
143:         timeout-minutes: ${{ fromJson(steps.test-timeout.outputs.timeout) }}
144:         env:
145:           BUILD_ENVIRONMENT: ${{ inputs.build-environment }}
146:           PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
147:           GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
148:           GITHUB_WORKFLOW: ${{ github.workflow }}
149:           GITHUB_JOB: ${{ github.job }}
150:           GITHUB_RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
151:           GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
152:           GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT: ${{ github.run_attempt }}
153:           JOB_ID: ${{ steps.get-job-id.outputs.job-id }}
154:           JOB_NAME: ${{ steps.get-job-id.outputs.job-name }}
155:           BRANCH: ${{ steps.parse-ref.outputs.branch }}
156:           SHA1: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
157:           BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.sha }}
158:           SHM_SIZE: '2g'
159:           DOCKER_IMAGE: ${{ inputs.docker-image }}
160:           VLLM_TEST_HUGGING_FACE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.VLLM_TEST_HUGGING_FACE_TOKEN }}
161:           HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN }}
162:           SCRIBE_GRAPHQL_ACCESS_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.SCRIBE_GRAPHQL_ACCESS_TOKEN }}
163:           ARTIFACTS_FILE_SUFFIX: ${{ github.job }}-${{ steps.get-job-id.outputs.job-id }}
164:         run: |
165:           set -x
166: 
167:           TEST_COMMAND=.ci/pytorch/test_fa3_abi_stable.sh
168: 
169:           # Leaving 1GB for the runner and other things
170:           TOTAL_AVAILABLE_MEMORY_IN_GB=$(awk '/MemTotal/ { printf "%.3f \n", $2/1024/1024 - 1 }' /proc/meminfo)
171:           # https://docs.docker.com/engine/containers/resource_constraints/#--memory-swap-details, the 3GB swap
172:           # comes from https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/pull/6058
173:           TOTAL_MEMORY_WITH_SWAP=$(("${TOTAL_AVAILABLE_MEMORY_IN_GB%.*}" + 3))
174: 
175: 
176:           SHM_OPTS="--shm-size=${SHM_SIZE}"
177:           JENKINS_USER="--user jenkins"
178:           DOCKER_SHELL_CMD=
179: 
180:           # detached container should get cleaned up by teardown_ec2_linux
181:           # TODO: Stop building test binaries as part of the build phase
182:           # Used for GPU_FLAG, SHM_OPTS, JENKINS_USER and DOCKER_SHELL_CMD since that doesn't play nice
183:           # shellcheck disable=SC2086,SC2090
184:           container_name=$(docker run \
185:             ${GPU_FLAG:-} \
186:             ${SCCACHE_SERVER_PORT_DOCKER_FLAG:-} \
187:             -e BUILD_ENVIRONMENT \
188:             -e PR_NUMBER \
189:             -e GITHUB_ACTIONS \
190:             -e GITHUB_REPOSITORY \
191:             -e GITHUB_WORKFLOW \
192:             -e GITHUB_JOB \
193:             -e GITHUB_RUN_ID \
194:             -e GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER \
195:             -e GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT \
196:             -e JOB_ID \
197:             -e JOB_NAME \
198:             -e BASE_SHA \
199:             -e BRANCH \
200:             -e SHA1 \
201:             -e MAX_JOBS="$(nproc --ignore=2)" \
202:             -e HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN \
203:             -e VLLM_TEST_HUGGING_FACE_TOKEN \
204:             -e SCRIBE_GRAPHQL_ACCESS_TOKEN \
205:             -e ARTIFACTS_FILE_SUFFIX \
206:             --memory="${TOTAL_AVAILABLE_MEMORY_IN_GB%.*}g" \
207:             --memory-swap="${TOTAL_MEMORY_WITH_SWAP}g" \
208:             --env-file="/tmp/github_env_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}" \
209:             --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \
210:             --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE \
211:             --ipc=host \
212:             ${SHM_OPTS} \
213:             --tty \
214:             --detach \
215:             --name="${container_name}" \
216:             ${JENKINS_USER} \
217:             -v "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}:/var/lib/jenkins/workspace" \
218:             -w /var/lib/jenkins/workspace \
219:             "${DOCKER_IMAGE}" \
220:             ${DOCKER_SHELL_CMD}
221:           )
222: 
223:           echo "DOCKER_CONTAINER_ID=${container_name}" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"
224: 
225:           docker exec -t "${container_name}" sh -c "python3 -m pip install $(echo dist/*.whl)[opt-einsum] && ${TEST_COMMAND}"
226: 
227:       - name: Collect backtraces from coredumps (if any)
228:         if: always()
229:         run: |
230:           # shellcheck disable=SC2156
231:           find . -iname "core.[1-9]*" -exec docker exec "${DOCKER_CONTAINER_ID}" sh -c "gdb python {} -ex 'bt' -ex 'q'" \;
232:

236:         with:
237:           name: coredumps-fa3-stable-abi-smoke-tests

241:

246:         with:

248:           job_name: ${{ steps.get-job-id.outputs.job-name }}

import json, os, re

# Store the raw content strings from the API responses

# _bazel-build-test.yml
files['.github/workflows/_bazel-build-test.yml'] = r"""name: bazel

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      build-environment:
        required: true
        type: string
        description: Top-level label for what's being built/tested.
      docker-image-name:
        required: true
        type: string
        description: Name of the base docker image to build with.
      cuda-version:
        required: true
        type: string
        description: What CUDA version to build with (i.e. "11.7"), "cpu" for none.
      sync-tag:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""
        description: |
          If this is set, our linter will use this to make sure that every other
          job with the same `sync-tag` is identical.
      test-matrix:
        required: true
        type: string
        description: |
          A JSON description of what configs to run later on.
      runner:
        required: false
        type: string
        default: "linux.large"
        description: Runner type

env:
  GIT_DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}

jobs:
  filter:
    if: github.repository_owner == 'pytorch'
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
    outputs:
      test-matrix: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.test-matrix }}
      is-test-matrix-empty: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.is-test-matrix-empty }}
      keep-going: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.keep-going }}
      reenabled-issues: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.reenabled-issues }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout PyTorch
        uses: pytorch/pytorch/.github/actions/checkout-pytorch@main
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1
          submodules: false

      - name: Select all requested test configurations
        id: filter
        uses: ./.github/actions/filter-test-configs
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          test-matrix: ${{ inputs.test-matrix }}

  build-and-test:
    needs: filter
    # Don't run on forked repos.
    if: github.repository_owner == 'pytorch' && needs.filter.outputs.is-test-matrix-empty == 'False'
    strategy:
      matrix: ${{ fromJSON(needs.filter.outputs.test-matrix) }}
      fail-fast: false
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    steps:
      - name: Setup SSH (Click me for login details)
        uses: pytorch/test-infra/.github/actions/setup-ssh@main
        with:
          github-secret: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      # [see note: pytorch repo ref]
      - name: Checkout PyTorch
        uses: pytorch/pytorch/.github/actions/checkout-pytorch@main

      - name: Setup Linux
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup-linux

      - name: Calculate docker image
        id: calculate-docker-image
        uses: pytorch/test-infra/.github/actions/calculate-docker-image@main
        with:
          docker-image-name: ${{ inputs.docker-image-name }}

      - name: Pull docker image
        uses: pytorch/test-infra/.github/actions/pull-docker-image@main
        with:
          docker-image: ${{ steps.calculate-docker-image.outputs.docker-image }}

      - name: Check if in a container runner
        shell: bash
        id: check_container_runner
        run: echo "IN_CONTAINER_RUNNER=$(if [ -f /.inarc ] || [ -f /.incontainer ]; then echo true ; else echo false; fi)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Install nvidia driver, nvidia-docker runtime, set GPU_FLAG
        uses: pytorch/test-infra/.github/actions/setup-nvidia@main

      - name: Output disk space left
        run: |
          sudo df -H

      - name: Preserve github env variables for use in docker
        run: |
          env | grep '^GITHUB' >> "/tmp/github_env_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"
          env | grep '^CI' >> "/tmp/github_env_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}"

      - name: Parse ref
        id: parse-ref
        run: .github/scripts/parse_ref.py

      - name: Get workflow job id
        id: get-job-id
        uses: ./.github/actions/get-workflow-job-id
        if: always()
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - name: Build
        env:
          BUILD_ENVIRONMENT: ${{ inputs.build-environment }}
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          BRANCH: ${{ steps.parse-ref.outputs.branch }}
          GITHUB_REPOSITORY: ${{ github.repository }}
          GITHUB_WORKFLOW: ${{ github.workflow }}
          GITHUB_JOB: ${{ github.job }}
          GITHUB_RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
          GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER: ${{ github.run_number }}
          GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT: ${{ github.run_attempt }}
          JOB_ID: ${{ steps.get-job-id.outputs.job-id }}
          REENABLED_ISSUES: ${{ needs.filter.outputs.reenabled-issues }}
          # TODO duplicated
          AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: us-east-1
          SHA1: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
          SCCACHE_BUCKET: ossci-compiler-cache-circleci-v2
          SCCACHE_REGION: us-east-1
          TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST: 5.2
          DOCKER_IMAGE: ${{ steps.calculate-docker-image.outputs.docker-image }}
          OUR_GITHUB_JOB_ID: ${{ steps.get-job-id.outputs.job-id }}
          CUDA_VERSION: ${{ inputs.cuda-version }}
        run: |
          export SHARD_NUMBER=0
          # detached container should get cleaned up by teardown_ec2_linux
          # TODO: Stop building test binaries as part of the build phase
          # Make sure we copy test results from bazel-testlogs symlink to
          # a regular directory ./test/test-reports
          # shellcheck disable=SC2086
          container_name=$(docker run \
            ${GPU_FLAG:-} \
            -e AWS_DEFAULT_REGION \
            -e BUILD_ENVIRONMENT \
            -e GITHUB_ACTIONS \
            -e GITHUB_REPOSITORY \
            -e GITHUB_WORKFLOW \
            -e GITHUB_JOB \
            -e GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER \
            -e GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT \
            -e JOB_ID \
            -e GIT_DEFAULT_BRANCH="$GIT_DEFAULT_BRANCH" \
            -e SHARD_NUMBER \
            -e NUM_TEST_SHARDS \
            -e MAX_JOBS="$(nproc --ignore=2)" \
            -e SCCACHE_BUCKET \
            -e SCCACHE_REGION \
            -e SKIP_SCCACHE_INITIALIZATION=1 \
            -e REENABLED_ISSUES \
            -e TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST \
            -e OUR_GITHUB_JOB_ID \
            -e CUDA_VERSION \
            --env-file="/tmp/github_env_${GITHUB_RUN_ID}" \
            --security-opt seccomp=unconfined \
            --cap-add=SYS_PTRACE \
            --shm-size="1g" \
            --tty \
            --detach \
            --user jenkins \
            -v "${GITHUB_WORKSPACE}:/var/lib/jenkins/workspace" \
            -w /var/lib/jenkins/workspace \
            "${DOCKER_IMAGE}"
          )
          docker exec -t "${container_name}" sh -c '.ci/pytorch/build.sh'
          echo "container_id=${container_name}" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"

      - name: Test
        id: test
        # Time out the test phase after 3.5 hours
        timeout-minutes: 120
        run: |
          docker exec -t "${container_id}" sh -c '.ci/pytorch/test.sh && cp -Lr ./bazel-testlogs ./test/test-reports'

      - name: Print remaining test logs
        shell: bash
        if: always() && steps.test.conclusion
        run: |
          cat test/**/*_toprint.log || true

      - name: Chown workspace
        uses: ./.github/actions/chown-workspace
        if: always()

      - name: Upload test artifacts
        uses: ./.github/actions/upload-test-artifacts
        if: always() && steps.test.conclusion && steps.test.conclusion != 'skipped'
        with:
          file-suffix: bazel-${{ github.job }}_${{ steps.get-job-id.outputs.job-id }}

      - name: Teardown Linux
        uses: pytorch/test-infra/.github/actions/teardown-linux@main
        if: always()
"""

for path, content in files.items():
    os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(f'/workspace/{path}'), exist_ok=True)
    with open(f'/workspace/{path}', 'w') as f:
        f.write(content)
    print(f'Written: {path}')

80:           """

87:           separated by a line containing "---".  If the line is not present, the
88:           settings are considered to be empty with only the second part, the user
89:           list, defined.

91:           The first part is a YAML block that defines the rollout settings. This can be
92:           used to define any settings that are needed to determine which runners to use.
93:           It's fields are defined by the RolloutSettings class below.

96:           The user list is also a comma separated list of additional features or
97:           experiments which the user could be opted in to.

102:           - Each user is also a comma-separated list of features/experiments to enable
103:           - A "#" prefix opts the user out of all experiments

116:                   default: true

119:               # Opt-ins:

121:               # and specifying experiments to enable in a comma-separated list.
122:               # To always opt out of an experiment, prefix it with a "-".

309:               # Fetch the actual username from the original PR. The PR number is
310:               # embedded in the tag name: ciflow/<name>/<pr-number>

312:               gh = get_gh_client(github_token)

314:               if username == "pytorch-bot[bot]" and ref_type == "tag":
315:                   split_tag = ref_name.split("/")
316:                   if (

350:           def extract_settings_user_opt_in_from_text(rollout_state: str) -> tuple[str, str]:
351:               """
352:               Extracts the text with settings, if any, and the opted in users from the rollout state.
353: 
354:               If the issue body contains "---" then the text above that is the settings
355:               and the text below is the list of opted in users.
356: 
357:               If it doesn't contain "---" then the settings are empty and the rest is the users.
358:               """
359:               rollout_state_parts = rollout_state.split("---")
360:               if len(rollout_state_parts) >= 2:
361:                   return rollout_state_parts[0], rollout_state_parts[1]
362:               else:

366:           class UserOptins(dict[str, list[str]]):

372:           def parse_user_opt_in_from_text(user_optin_text: str) -> UserOptins:
373:               """
374:               Parse the user opt-in text into a key value pair of username and the list of features they have opted into
375: 
376:               Users are GitHub usernames with the @ prefix. Each user is also a comma-separated list of features/experiments to enable.
377:                   - Example line: "@User1,lf,split_build"
378:                   - A "#" prefix indicates the user is opted out of all experiments
379: 
380: 
381:               """
382:               optins = UserOptins()
383:               for user in user_optin_text.split("\n"):
384:                   user = user.strip("\r\n\t -")
385:                   if not user or not user.startswith("@"):
386:                       # Not a valid user. Skip
387:                       continue
388: 
389:                   if user:
390:                       usr_name = user.split(",")[0].strip("@")
391:                       optins[usr_name] = [exp.strip(" ") for exp in user.split(",")[1:]]
392: 
393:               return optins
394: 
395: 
396:           def is_valid_experiment_name(experiment_name: str) -> bool:
397:               """
398:               Check if the experiment name is valid.
399:               A valid name:
400:                   - Contains only alphanumeric characters and the special characters "_" & "-"
401:                   - The special characters "_" & "-" shouldn't be the first or last characters
402:                   - Cannot contain spaces
403:               """
404: 
405:               valid_char_regex = r"^[a-zA-Z0-9]([\w-]*[a-zA-Z0-9])?$"
406:               valid = bool(re.match(valid_char_regex, experiment_name))
407: 
408:               if valid:
409:                   return True
410: 
411:               log.error(
412:                   f"Invalid experiment name: {experiment_name}. Experiment names should only contain alphanumeric characters, '_', and '-'. They cannot contain spaces, and the special characters '_' and '-' cannot be the first or last characters."
413:               )
414:               return False
415: 
416: 
417:           def parse_settings_from_text(settings_text: str) -> Settings:
418:               """
419:               Parse the experiments from the issue body into a list of ExperimentSettings
420:               """
421:               try:
422:                   if settings_text:
423:                       # Escape the backtick as well so that we can have the settings in a code block on the GH issue
424:                       # for easy reading
425:                       # Note: Using ascii for the backtick so that the cat step in _runner-determinator.yml doesn't choke on
426:                       #       the backtick character in shell commands.
427:                       backtick = chr(96)  # backtick character
428:                       settings_text = settings_text.strip(f"\r\n\t{backtick} ")
429:                       settings = load_yaml(settings_text)
430: 
431:                       # For now we just load experiments. We can expand this if/when we add more settings
432:                       experiments = {}
433: 
434:                       for exp_name, exp_settings in settings.get(SETTING_EXPERIMENTS).items():
435:                           if not is_valid_experiment_name(exp_name):
436:                               # Exclude invalid experiments from the list. We log an error, but don't raise an exception so that other experiments can still be processed.
437:                               continue
438: 
439:                           valid_settings = {}
440:                           for setting in exp_settings:
441:                               if setting not in Experiment._fields:
442:                                   log.warning(
443:                                       f"Unexpected setting in experiment: {setting} = {exp_settings[setting]}"
444:                                   )
445:                               else:
446:                                   valid_settings[setting] = exp_settings[setting]
447: 
448:                           experiments[exp_name] = Experiment(**valid_settings)
449:                       return Settings(experiments)
450: 
451:               except Exception:
452:                   log.exception("Failed to parse settings")
453: 
454:               return Settings()
455: 
456: 
457:           def parse_settings(rollout_state: str) -> Settings:
458:               """
459:               Parse settings, if any, from the rollout state.
460: 
461:               If the issue body contains "---" then the text above that is the settings
462:               and the text below is the list of opted in users.
463: 
464:               If it doesn't contain "---" then the settings are empty and the default values are used.
465:               """
466:               settings_text, _ = extract_settings_user_opt_in_from_text(rollout_state)
467:               return parse_settings_from_text(settings_text)
468: 
469: 
470:           def parse_users(rollout_state: str) -> UserOptins:
471:               """
472:               Parse users from the rollout state.
473: 
474:               """
475:               _, users_text = extract_settings_user_opt_in_from_text(rollout_state)
476:               return parse_user_opt_in_from_text(users_text)
477: 
478: 
479:           def is_user_opted_in(user: str, user_optins: UserOptins, experiment_name: str) -> bool:
480:               """
481:               Check if a user is opted into an experiment
482:               """
483:               return experiment_name in user_optins.get(user, [])
484: 
485: 
486:           def is_user_opted_out(user: str, user_optins: UserOptins, experiment_name: str) -> bool:
487:               """
488:               Check if a user explicitly opted out of an experiment
489:               """
490:               # if the experiment is prefixed with a "-", then it's an opt-out
491:               experiment_optout = "-" + experiment_name
492:               if experiment_optout not in user_optins.get(user, []):
493:                   return False
494: 
495:               if is_user_opted_in(user, user_optins, experiment_name):
496:                   log.warning(
497:                       f"User {user} is opted into experiment {experiment_name}, but also opted out of it. Defaulting to opting out"
498:                   )
499: 
500:               return True
501: 
502: 
503:           def get_runner_prefix(
504:               rollout_state: str,
505:               workflow_requestors: Iterable[str],
506:               branch: str,
507:               eligible_experiments: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
508:               opt_out_experiments: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
509:               is_canary: bool = False,
510:           ) -> str:
511:               settings = parse_settings(rollout_state)
512:               user_optins = parse_users(rollout_state)
513: 
514:               fleet_prefix = ""
515:               prefixes = []
516:               for experiment_name, experiment_settings in settings.experiments.items():
517:                   if not experiment_settings.all_branches and is_exception_branch(branch):
518:                       log.info(
519:                           f"Branch {branch} is an exception branch. Not enabling experiment {experiment_name}."
520:                       )
521:                       continue
522: 
523:                   if opt_out_experiments:
524:                       if experiment_name in opt_out_experiments:
525:                           opt_out_exp_list = ", ".join(opt_out_experiments)
526:                           log.info(
527:                               f"Skipping experiment '{experiment_name}', as this workflow has opted-out (opted out experiments are: {opt_out_exp_list})"
528:                           )
529:                           continue
530: 
531:                   if eligible_experiments:
532:                       if experiment_name not in eligible_experiments:
533:                           exp_list = ", ".join(eligible_experiments)
534:                           log.info(
535:                               f"Skipping experiment '{experiment_name}', as it is not in the eligible_experiments list: {exp_list}"
536:                           )
537:                           continue
538:                   elif not experiment_settings.default:
539:                       log.info(
540:                           f"Skipping experiment '{experiment_name}', as it is not a default experiment"
541:                       )
542:                       continue
543: 
544:                   # Is any workflow_requestor opted out to this experiment?
545:                   opted_out_users = [
546:                       requestor
547:                       for requestor in workflow_requestors
548:                       if is_user_opted_out(requestor, user_optins, experiment_name)
549:                   ]
550: 
551:                   if opted_out_users:
552:                       log.info(
553:                           f"{', '.join(opted_out_users)} have opted out of experiment {experiment_name}."
554:                       )
555:                       continue
556: 
557:                   # Is any workflow_requestor opted in to this experiment?
558:                   opted_in_users = [
559:                       requestor
560:                       for requestor in workflow_requestors
561:                       if is_user_opted_in(requestor, user_optins, experiment_name)
562:                   ]
563: 
564:                   enabled = False
565:                   if opted_in_users:
566:                       log.info(
567:                           f"{', '.join(opted_in_users)} have opted into experiment {experiment_name}."
568:                       )
569:                       enabled = True
570: 
571:                   elif experiment_settings.rollout_perc:
572:                       # If no user is opted in, then we randomly enable the experiment based on the rollout percentage
573:                       if random.uniform(0, 100) <= experiment_settings.rollout_perc:
574:                           log.info(
575:                               f"Based on rollout percentage of {experiment_settings.rollout_perc}%, enabling experiment {experiment_name}."
576:                           )
577:                           enabled = True
578: 
579:                   if enabled:
580:                       label = experiment_name
581:                       if experiment_name == LF_FLEET_EXPERIMENT:
582:                           # We give some special treatment to the "lf" experiment since determines the fleet we use
583:                           #  - If it's enabled, then we always list it's prefix first
584:                           #  - If we're in the canary branch, then we append ".c" to the lf prefix
585:                           if is_canary:
586:                               label += CANARY_FLEET_SUFFIX
587:                           fleet_prefix = label
588:                       else:
589:                           prefixes.append(label)
590: 
591:               if len(prefixes) > 1:
592:                   log.error(
593:                       f"Only a fleet and one other experiment can be enabled for a job at any time. Enabling {prefixes[0]} and ignoring the rest, which are {', '.join(prefixes[1:])}"
594:                   )
595:                   prefixes = prefixes[:1]
596: 
597:               # Fleet always comes first
598:               if fleet_prefix:
599:                   prefixes.insert(0, fleet_prefix)
600: 
601:               return ".".join(prefixes) + "." if prefixes else ""
602: 
603: 
604:           def get_rollout_state_from_issue(github_token: str, repo: str, issue_num: int) -> str:
605:               """
606:               Gets the first comment of the issue, which contains the desired rollout state.
607: 
608:               The default issue we use - https://github.com/pytorch/test-infra/issues/5132
609:               """
610:               gh = get_gh_client(github_token)
611:               issue = get_issue(gh, repo, issue_num)
612:               return str(issue.get_comments()[0].body.strip("\n\t "))
613: 
614: 
615:           def download_json(url: str, headers: dict[str, str], num_retries: int = 3) -> Any:
616:               for _ in range(num_retries):
617:                   try:
618:                       req = Request(url=url, headers=headers)
619:                       content = urlopen(req, timeout=5).read().decode("utf-8")
620:                       return json.loads(content)
621:                   except Exception as e:
622:                       log.warning(f"Could not download {url}: {e}")
623: 
624:               log.warning(f"All {num_retries} retries exhausted, downloading {url} failed")
625:               return {}
626: 
627: 
628:           @cache
629:           def get_pr_info(github_repo: str, github_token: str, pr_number: int) -> dict[str, Any]:
630:               """
631:               Dynamically get PR information
632:               """
633:               github_api = f"https://api.github.com/repos/{github_repo}"
634:               headers = {
635:                   "Accept": "application/vnd.github.v3+json",
636:                   "Authorization": f"token {github_token}",
637:               }
638:               json_response: dict[str, Any] = download_json(
639:                   url=f"{github_api}/issues/{pr_number}",
640:                   headers=headers,
641:               )
642: 
643:               if not json_response:
644:                   log.warning(f"Failed to get the labels for #{pr_number}")
645:                   return {}
646: 
647:               return json_response
648: 
649: 
650:           def get_labels(github_repo: str, github_token: str, pr_number: int) -> set[str]:
651:               """
652:               Dynamically get the latest list of labels from the pull request
653:               """
654:               pr_info = get_pr_info(github_repo, github_token, pr_number)
655:               return {
656:                   label.get("name") for label in pr_info.get("labels", []) if label.get("name")
657:               }
658: 
659: 
660:           def main() -> None:
661:               args = parse_args()
662: 
663:               runner_label_prefix = DEFAULT_LABEL_PREFIX
664: 
665:               # Check if the PR is opt-out
666:               if args.pr_number:
667:                   labels = get_labels(args.github_repo, args.github_token, int(args.pr_number))
668:                   if OPT_OUT_LABEL in labels:
669:                       log.info(
670:                           f"Opt-out runner determinator because #{args.pr_number} has {OPT_OUT_LABEL} label"
671:                       )
672:                       set_github_output(GH_OUTPUT_KEY_LABEL_TYPE, runner_label_prefix)
673:                       sys.exit()
674: 
675:               try:
676:                   rollout_state = get_rollout_state_from_issue(
677:                       args.github_token, args.github_issue_repo, args.github_issue
678:                   )
679: 
680:                   username = get_potential_pr_author(
681:                       args.github_token,
682:                       args.github_repo,
683:                       args.github_actor,
684:                       args.github_ref_type,
685:                       args.github_branch,
686:                   )
687: 
688:                   is_canary = args.github_repo == "pytorch/pytorch-canary"
689: 
690:                   runner_label_prefix = get_runner_prefix(
691:                       rollout_state,
692:                       (args.github_issue_owner, username),
693:                       args.github_branch,
694:                       args.eligible_experiments,
695:                       args.opt_out_experiments,
696:                       is_canary,
697:                   )
698: 
699:               except Exception as e:
700:                   log.error(
701:                       f"Failed to get issue. Defaulting to Meta runners and no experiments. Exception: {e}"
702:                   )
703: 
704:               set_github_output(GH_OUTPUT_KEY_LABEL_TYPE, runner_label_prefix)
705: 
706: 
707:           if __name__ == "__main__":
708:               main()
709: 
710:           EOF

29:         required: false
30:         type: boolean
31:         default: false
32:         description: If set, build in debug mode.

34:         required: false
35:         type: string
36:         default: ""

38:           If this is set, our linter will use this to make sure that every other
39:           job with the same `sync-tag` is identical.
40:       test-matrix:
41:         required: false
42:         type: string
43:         description: |
44:           An option JSON description of what test configs to run later on. This
45:           is moved here from the Linux test workflow so that we can apply filter
46:           logic using test-config labels earlier and skip unnecessary builds
47:       runner:
48:         required: false
49:         type: string
50:         default: "windows.4xlarge.nonephemeral"
51:         description: |
52:           Label of the runner this job should run on.
53: 
54:     outputs:
55:       test-matrix:
56:         value: ${{ jobs.build.outputs.test-matrix }}
57:         description: An optional JSON description of what test configs to run later on.
58:       build-environment:
59:         value: ${{ jobs.build.outputs.build-environment }}
60:         description: Top-level label for what's being built/tested.
61: 
62: env:
63:   GIT_DEFAULT_BRANCH: ${{ github.event.repository.default_branch }}
64: 
65: jobs:
66:   build:
67:     # Don't run on forked repos.
68:     if: github.repository_owner == 'pytorch'
69:     runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner }}
70:     timeout-minutes: 240
71:     outputs:
72:       test-matrix: ${{ steps.filter.outputs.test-matrix }}
73:       build-environment: ${{ inputs.build-environment }}
74:     defaults:
75:       run:
76:         shell: bash
77:     steps:
78:       # Duplicated in win-test because this MUST go before a checkout
79:       - name: Enable git long paths and symlinks on Windows and disable fsmonitor daemon
80:         shell: bash
81:         run: |
82:           git config --global core.longpaths true
83:           git config --global core.symlinks true
84:           git config --global core.ignorecase false
85: 
86:           # https://git-scm.com/docs/git-fsmonitor--daemon.  The daemon could lock
87:           # the directory on Windows and prevent GHA from checking out as reported
88:           # in https://github.com/actions/checkout/issues/1018
89:           git config --global core.fsmonitor false
90: 
91:       - name: Setup SSH (Click me for login details)
92:         uses: pytorch/test-infra/.github/actions/setup-ssh@main
93:         with:
94:           github-secret: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
95:           instructions: |
96:             To forward remote desktop on your local machine ssh as follows:
97:               ssh -L 3389:localhost:3389 %%username%%@%%hostname%%
98:             And then change password using `passwd` command.
99: 
100:             To start build locally, change working folder to \actions-runner\_work\pytorch\pytorch,
101:             Activate miniconda and Visual Studio environment, by running:
102:               call C:\Jenkins\Miniconda3\Scripts\activate.bat C:\Jenkins\Miniconda3
103:               call "C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft Visual Studio\2022\BuildTools\VC\Auxiliary\Build\vcvarsall.bat" x64
104: 
105:       # [see note: pytorch repo ref]
106:       - name: Checkout PyTorch
107:         uses: pytorch/pytorch/.github/actions/checkout-pytorch@main
108:         with:
109:           no-sudo: true
110: 
111:       - name: Setup Windows

113:         with:
114:           cuda-version: ${{ inputs.cuda-version }}
115: 
116:       - name: Parse ref
117:         id: parse-ref

120: 
121:       - name: Get workflow job id
122:         id: get-job-id
123:         uses: ./.github/actions/get-workflow-job-id
124:         if: always()
125:         with:
126:           github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
127:

129:       - name: Select all requested test configurations (if the test matrix is available)

137:       - name: Download pytest cache

142:           job_identifier: ${{ github.workflow }}_${{ inputs.build-environment }}

145:         if: steps.filter.outputs.is-test-matrix-empty == 'False' || inputs.test-matrix == ''
146:         id: build
147:         shell: bash
148:         env:
149:           PYTORCH_FINAL_PACKAGE_DIR: /c/${{ github.run_id }}/build-results/
150:           BRANCH: ${{ steps.parse-ref.outputs.branch }}
151:           BUILD_ENVIRONMENT: ${{ inputs.build-environment }}
152:           BUILD_WHEEL: 1
153:           MAX_JOBS: 8
154:           CUDA_VERSION: ${{ inputs.cuda-version }}
155:           PYTHON_VERSION: "3.10"
156:           SCCACHE_BUCKET: "ossci-compiler-cache"
157:           SCCACHE_S3_KEY_PREFIX: ${{ github.workflow }}
158:           SCCACHE_REGION: us-east-1
159:           VC_PRODUCT: "BuildTools"
160:           VC_VERSION: ""
161:           VC_YEAR: "${{ inputs.vc-year }}"
162:           ALPINE_IMAGE: "308535385114.dkr.ecr.us-east-1.amazonaws.com/tool/alpine"
163:           AWS_DEFAULT_REGION: us-east-1
164:           PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
165:           SHA1: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
166:           DEBUG: ${{ inputs.build-with-debug && '1' || '0' }}
167:           TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST: "8.6"
168:           USE_CUDA: ${{ inputs.cuda-version != 'cpu' && '1' || '0' }}
169:           USE_XPU: ${{ inputs.use-xpu == true && '1' || '0' }}
170:           XPU_VERSION: "${{ inputs.xpu-version }}"
171:           OUR_GITHUB_JOB_ID: ${{ steps.get-job-id.outputs.job-id }}
172:         run: |
173:           .ci/pytorch/win-build.sh
174: 
175:       # Collect Windows torch libs and CUDA libs for cross-compilation
176:       - name: Collect Windows CUDA libs for cross-compilation
177:         if: steps.build.outcome != 'skipped' && inputs.cuda-version != 'cpu'
178:         shell: bash
179:         run: |
180:           set -ex
181: 
182:           # Create directory structure if does not exist
183:           mkdir -p /c/${{ github.run_id }}/build-results
184: 
185:           # Copy CUDA libs
186:           CUDA_PATH="/c/Program Files/NVIDIA GPU Computing Toolkit/CUDA/v${{ inputs.cuda-version }}"
187: 
188:           if [ -f "${CUDA_PATH}/lib/x64/cuda.lib" ]; then
189:             cp "${CUDA_PATH}/lib/x64/cuda.lib" /c/${{ github.run_id }}/build-results/
190:           fi
191: 
192:           if [ -f "${CUDA_PATH}/lib/x64/cudart.lib" ]; then
193:             cp "${CUDA_PATH}/lib/x64/cudart.lib" /c/${{ github.run_id }}/build-results/
194:           fi
195: 
196:           # List collected files
197:           echo "Collected CUDA libs:"
198:           ls -lah /c/${{ github.run_id }}/build-results/*.lib
199: 
200:       # Upload to github so that people can click and download artifacts
201:       - name: Upload artifacts to s3
202:         if: steps.build.outcome != 'skipped'
203:         uses: seemethere/upload-artifact-s3@baba72d0712b404f646cebe0730933554ebce96a # v5.1.0
204:         with:
205:           retention-days: 14
206:           if-no-files-found: error
207:           name: ${{ inputs.build-environment }}
208:           path: C:\${{ github.run_id }}\build-results
209: 
210:       - name: Upload sccache stats
211:         if: steps.build.outcome != 'skipped'
212:         uses: ./.github/actions/upload-sccache-stats
213:         with:
214:           github-token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
215: 
216:       - name: Teardown Windows
217:         uses: ./.github/actions/teardown-win
218:         if: always()
219:         timeout-minutes: 120
220:         with:
221:           extra-delete-dir: /c/${{ github.run_id }}/build-results/
